# Preparing External Files

Several static input files must be generated or copied before the model can run.
This step assumes MSCPROGS and hycom_ALL have been compiled successfully.

## Relaxation, river forcing, and MPI tile definition files

These files are generated by `create_ref_case.sh`. Copy the script to your experiment
directory:

```bash
cd $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/expt_<EXPT_ID>
cp $HOME/NERSC-HYCOM-CICE/bin/create_ref_case.sh .
```

Open `create_ref_case.sh` and update:

- `Icore` — number of MPI tiles in the i-direction (e.g. `29` for TP2)
- `Jcore` — number of MPI tiles in the j-direction (e.g. `26` for TP2)
- `iceclim` — set to `0` (no ice climatology) or `1` (initialize from ice climatology)

Also find the `tile_grid.sh` call and add the `-s 1` flag, which gives extra flexibility
in the tiling:

```bash
tile_grid.sh -s 1 -${Icore} -${Jcore} ${T} > $EDIR/log/ref_tiling.out 2>&1
```

Then run the script:

```bash
bash create_ref_case.sh
```

This generates the following files:

**Under `$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/relax/<IEXPT>/`:**
- Physics relaxation climatology (z-level and hybrid-level)
- BGC relaxation climatology (z-level and hybrid-level) — when `ntracr ≠ 0`
- CO2 relaxation climatology — when `ntracr ≠ 0`
- Relaxation mask
- Sea ice cover climatology — when `ICECLIM=1`

**Under `$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/force/rivers/<IEXPT>/`:**
- River forcing

**Under `$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/force/seawifs/`:**
- kpar forcing

**Under `$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/topo/partit/`:**
- MPI tile definition files, e.g. `depth_TP2a0.10_04.0504` and `depth_TP2a0.10_04.0504.ppm`

The four-digit number `0504` in the tile file name indicates that `NMPI` should be set to
`504` in `EXPT.src`. Update `NMPI` accordingly if your tiling generates a different number.

## Nesting timescale definition files

When nesting is enabled in `blkdat.input`, the following files must be present under
`$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/nest/<IEXPT>/`:

- `ports.input`
- `rmu.a` / `rmu.b`
- `rmutr.a` / `rmutr.b`

For TP2, copy them from the reference experiment:

```bash
DIR_NST=/nird/datalake/NS9481K/shuang/nest/TP2_expt023
mkdir -p $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/nest/<IEXPT>
cd $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/nest/<IEXPT>
cp ${DIR_NST}/ports.input .
cp ${DIR_NST}/rmu.a ${DIR_NST}/rmu.b .
cp ${DIR_NST}/rmutr.a ${DIR_NST}/rmutr.b .
```

## Sponge layer diffusion files

If sponge layers are enabled (i.e. `thkdf4` and `veldf4` are negative in `blkdat.input`),
the following files must be present under `$WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/relax/<IEXPT>/`:

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `rmu.[a,b]` | 2D relaxation timescale for physics |
| `rmutr.[a,b]` | 2D relaxation timescale for BGC |
| `thkdf4.[a,b]` | 2D biharmonic diffusion coefficient for layer thickness |
| `veldf4.[a,b]` | 2D biharmonic diffusion coefficient for velocity |

These are generated by `$BIN_HYCOM/hycom_creat_thkdf4_veldf4.py`.

First, create a scratch directory and link in the grid and topography files:

```bash
mkdir -p $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/relax/<IEXPT>/SCRATCH
cd $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/relax/<IEXPT>/SCRATCH
ln -sf $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/topo/regional.grid.a .
ln -sf $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/topo/regional.grid.b .
ln -sf $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/topo/regional.depth.a .
ln -sf $WORK/<CONFIGNAME>/topo/regional.depth.b .
```

Copy the script locally:

```bash
cp $BIN_HYCOM/hycom_creat_thkdf4_veldf4.py .
```

Open the script and set the parameters for your configuration:

| Parameter | TP2 | TP5 | Description |
|-----------|-----|-----|-------------|
| `mnn` | `0.05` | `0.02` | Minimum diffusion value |
| `mxx` | `0.125` | `0.125` | Maximum diffusion value |

Then run the script with the sponge layer width as its argument (20 grid cells for TP2):

```bash
python hycom_creat_thkdf4_veldf4.py 20
```

Copy the output to the parent directory:

```bash
cp thkdf4.a thkdf4.b veldf4.a veldf4.b ../
```
